Attitudes toward coal development at Sarpy Creek of Hardin residents and Ranchers residing in the Sarpy Creek area were surveyed in 1975 by Mountain West Research (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 e). Over 80 percent of 64 Hardin residents faced with the hypothetical decision of developing or not developing the Sarpy Creek mine indicated in favor of development, citing energy needs (42.2%), economic benefits (35.9%) and environmental benefits (10.9%) as the major reasons.
Approximately 80 percent of the persons in nine ranching families interviewed felt mining to be incompatible with ranching and farming activities and lifestyle, with the remaining 20 percent noncomittal. The most frequent comments related to the influx of people, pollution and traffic, blasting effects, social disruption and changes in the landscape.
Tribal Organization
The Crow Tribe adopted a written constitution on June 24, 1948, which was approved on May 23, 1949 by the Secretary of the Interior. The Constitution calls for elections of a Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Secretary, and Vice-Secretary every two years.
The principal duty of the four major officials is to carry out the directives of the Crow Tribal Council. All enrolled tribal members are official members of the Crow Tribal Council, provided the females are 18 years of age or older and the males 21 years old or over. Members of the Tribal Council are empowered to propose resolutions before the council and to engage in discussions and deliberations at council meetings.
